description: Language edits to the FAQ answers, applied by build_faq_data.py after the answers are read from docs/sources. Each 'old' passage must occur exactly once in the answer. The edits fix grammar, punctuation, British spelling and consistent terms (the Agency, handicaptillæg, 'you'), and remove em dashes. They do not change what an answer says. 2026-11-06.

edits.old:
As a starting point, an impairment is permanent when it is not expected to improve substantially, either on its own or through treatment, within a longer number of years. Some non-exhaustive examples are:

permanent physical impairments include severe muscle or nerve conditions (e.g. muscular dystrophy, MS, severe spinal conditions, cerebral palsy),

blindness or severe visual impairment, and

deafness or severe hearing impairment.

Permanent mental impairments can include:

severe psychological difficulties due to personality disorder, eating disorder, OCD or anxiety,

schizophrenia-spectrum disorders,

affective disorders (including bipolar disorder and recurrent depression),

and ADHD or autism spectrum disorder.

Having one of these conditions does not by itself guarantee approval, and conditions outside this list can also qualify — the list is not exhaustive.
edits.new:
As a starting point, an impairment is permanent when it is not expected to improve substantially, either on its own or through treatment, within a period of several years. Some examples follow; neither list is exhaustive.

Permanent physical impairments can include severe muscle or nerve conditions (e.g. muscular dystrophy, MS, severe spinal conditions, cerebral palsy), blindness or severe visual impairment, and deafness or severe hearing impairment.

Permanent mental impairments can include severe psychological difficulties due to personality disorder, eating disorder, OCD or anxiety; schizophrenia-spectrum disorders; affective disorders (including bipolar disorder and recurrent depression); and ADHD or autism spectrum disorder.

Having one of these conditions does not by itself guarantee approval, and conditions that are not listed can also qualify.

edits.why: grammar and word order throughout; American spelling 'recognized'
edits.old:
If your documentation does not show that you have a permanent impairment, you will be likely denied. This is the case, if you for example apply on the basis of a condition that is by definition not permanent, such as a single surgery, a single period of sickness, a broken arm or pregnancy related issues where the most people will recover completely in a relatively short time period. You can also not apply if you are only sick for a short period of time because you for example are registered as sick for 2 months in relation with a surgery.

There might be exceptions for non-permanent impairments that might be able to be recognized as permanent when having persisted for a longer period.
edits.new:
If your documentation does not show that you have a permanent impairment, you will likely be denied. This is the case if, for example, you apply on the basis of a condition that is by definition not permanent, such as a single operation, a single period of illness, a broken arm or pregnancy-related issues, where most people recover completely within a relatively short time. Nor can you apply if you are only ill for a short period, for example if you are on sick leave for 2 months in connection with an operation.

There may be exceptions: a condition that is not permanent can in some cases be recognised as permanent once it has lasted for a longer period.
